newsitem.title: USA: Schawk sees 20-30 pct revenue growth.
newsitem.headline: Schawk sees 20-30 pct revenue growth.

text.p: Schawk Inc on Wednesday said it expected 1997 revenue growth of between 20 and 30 percent.
"Our performance outlook for 1997 is good," Marie Graul, chief financial officer, said in a statement.
Graul said 1997 sales were expected to reach about $115 million, net income should grow at a double-digit pace and operating margins should expand into the mid-teens.
She also said Schawk, which is closely held, is evaluating ways to enhance market liquidity and expand its average trading volume.
Schawk posted 1996 operating profit of $0.22 a share and a net loss of $1.34. Its sales last year totaled $90.8 million.

"Since last year, we've enhanced our position in the imaging technology market," Clarence Schawk, chairman, said in a statement. "Our strong balance sheet enables us to enjoy the prospect of numerous potential acquisition opportunities to help drive our growth."

Speaking at the company's annual meeting Wednesday, Schawk also said the company aims to achieve a 20 percent share of the worldwide market for packaging imaging and a 10 percent share of the overall imaging market within the next few years.

He said the company's strategy for reaching this goal involves expanding its international presence through affiliations, continuing to capitalize on high-margin acquisitions and developing additional value-added services.
